paragraphs: Bedfordshire has no single county fostering service. Bedford Borough Council and Central Bedfordshire Council each recruit and support their own foster carers, and both direct enquiries through Foster East, a regional recruitment service. The services listed on this page are independent agencies that also place children across the county.

Central Bedfordshire said in a 2024 appeal that it was looking after 362 children in care and worked with 119 foster families, and that it was short of carers. The council pays a weekly child allowance by age, from £189 for under-fives to £278 for young people aged 16 and over, plus a weekly carer fee of £100 in the first two years of fostering and £175 after that. It adds a £1,000 welcome payment for newly approved mainstream carers, holiday and birthday allowances, and a £500 long-service payment every five years. Our Central Bedfordshire allowance page sets out the full scale.

Bedford Borough Council says almost anyone can foster: single people, couples, LGBTQIA+ people, people in or out of work, homeowners and renters. You need to be over 21 and have a spare bedroom for any child over three. It offers training, support, an allowance for the child and a fee for the carer, but does not publish its rates on the pages we read.

Because the two councils and the agencies below pay and support carers differently, it is worth speaking to two or three of them before you apply and asking about fees, training and local support groups.
